# Capstone Part 2: Build and Integrate

## Overview
With a solid plan from Part 1, Part 2 is where you construct the automation, applying the full range of skills from the previous weeks in a realistic, integrated build - this is the hands-on core of your capstone. You work from your design, building it up incrementally rather than all at once: start with the trigger and get it firing on real (or realistic test) data, then add and verify one integration at a time - authenticate each app securely (Day 13), map and transform the data between them (Day 17), and confirm each step works before moving on. Building incrementally and testing as you go is far easier to debug than wiring everything up and hoping. You implement the logic your design calls for - filters and branches for decisions, iterators/aggregators for lists, a database for state and deduplication (Day 25), and, where appropriate, an AI step for classification or extraction (Day 26). Crucially, you do not treat reliability and security as afterthoughts: you build in error handling and retries (Day 18), validate inputs, secure credentials and webhooks (Day 30), and follow the design and documentation best practices from Day 35 so the result is modular and maintainable, not a fragile tangle. Throughout, you iterate with test data, deliberately throwing edge cases at it (Day 29) and fixing what breaks, keeping your work in version control (Day 28) and exporting the workflow. By the end of Part 2 you should have a functioning, integrated automation that handles the real process on test data, complete with error handling and security - essentially a working system that just needs final deployment, monitoring, and polish in Part 3. This build is the centerpiece that demonstrates you can turn a plan into a real, reliable automation.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Building the main workflow from the plan; Integrating each system and authenticating; Implementing data transformation and logic; Adding error handling and security; Iterating with test data. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
**Practical Task:** Build the core of your capstone: implement the trigger and at least the first two integrations end to end on test data, with authentication, data mapping, and a first pass of error handling in place.
**Mini Project:** Complete the full capstone build: all systems integrated, logic and data transformations implemented, a database for state/dedup, error handling and security applied, and the whole workflow verified against a set of normal and edge-case test inputs.
**Assignment:** Document your build process, including one significant problem you hit while integrating a system and exactly how you diagnosed and solved it.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
